ego.name: Herman Hollerith
ego.summary: German-American statistician, inventor, and businessman who pioneered electromechanical punched-card tabulation, first used at scale for U.S. census processing. He founded the Tabulating Machine Company, which was later amalgamated into the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company (CTR), renamed IBM in 1924.

category_summaries.summary: Family detail is limited in the provided extract: Georg Hollerith is central early on, while later descendants appear mainly through archival references.
Professional ties dominate: Billings as a key early influence, census administrators tied to the 1890/1900 deployments, and CTR leaders involved in the 1911 merger and its aftermath.
A small set of posthumous links (like Brian Randell’s 1982 republication) reflects how Hollerith’s work was curated into computing history.
